lens: Deployability and operability: the environment model, migrations, staging, rollback, secret rotation, cron ownership, health and synthetic checks, error tracking, the Vercel/Docker split, and how long a cold-start engineer needs to deploy safely.
strengths: lib/env.ts is the strongest operational artifact in the repo. 48 keys validated once at module load, with cross-field refinements that encode real incidents rather than theory: NOTIFY_DRIVER=fake is refused against the supabase driver because it records sends that never happened (lib/env.ts:246-253), the committed dev password is refused in production (lib/env.ts:310-316), and an ephemeral data driver is refused in production (lib/env.ts:317-323). A misconfigured deploy fails at boot instead of on a guest's first playback request. The eslint rule confining process.env to this one file is what makes that guarantee hold.

The synthetic guest check is better than most funded startups have. app/api/cron/synthetic/route.ts:52-91 walks resolve -> load bundle -> find a ready film -> mint a playback token against real production data, returns 503 when a step fails, and emails. Its own doc comment (lines 16-20) states the reason precisely: /api/health stayed green through every real fault this product has had. It deliberately stops before fetching the CDN manifest so a Bunny edge hiccup does not page you about your own app.

Scheduled jobs leave a durable record. lib/jobs/run.ts:18-46 wraps every cron, supabase/migrations/0022_job_runs.sql stores one row per run, and lib/health/probes.ts:165-193 turns 'did the drain run last night' into a sentence with an overdue threshold of 1.5x the declared cadence. Most teams build this only after an incident.

scripts/preflight.ts is a genuinely excellent pre-deploy gate. It distinguishes a Bunny account key from a library key and explains the difference (lines 138-146), checks that the pull zone actually enforces token authentication rather than that the key merely exists (lines 240-247), catches BlockNoneReferrer and IP pinning, and round-trips a real photo write -> CDN read -> delete using a fresh cache key each run because a fixed key was served from the CDN cache and produced a false failure (lines 300-310).

scripts/deploy-vercel.sh:47-63 refuses to link to a Vercel project that does not already exist, because `vercel link --yes` once created a second empty project and deployed into it while production kept serving the old build. A past incident encoded as a guard, with the reasoning kept next to it.

CI is hermetic by construction. .github/workflows/ci.yml:13-18 runs on the memory and fake drivers so no third party's uptime can flake the pipeline, and gates lint, typecheck, 659 tests, knip dead-code, the contrast gate, the build, a first-load JS budget and a real Core Web Vitals measurement. The comment at ci.yml:48-56 records that a decorative test-reporter step was silently skipping five real gates for days, and it was found and removed rather than muted.

lib/observability.ts is a correctly shaped seam: setErrorSink swaps in a vendor with zero call-site changes, and lib/log.ts:12-26 redacts secret-shaped keys centrally instead of trusting every call site. Adding Sentry is genuinely one file.

The backlog is honest about the gaps. docs/NEXT.md:181-194 (N-87 staging, labelled 'debt that is costing us') and the error-tracking item at docs/NEXT.md:271-273 already name two of this review's findings with costs attached. docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:114 states plainly that there is no migration ledger. Nothing here should be news to the author.

findings.title: All alerting runs through a queue drained by a scheduler that disables itself after 60 days of repo inactivity
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/notify-drain.yml:14-15 states the rule in its own header: 'A public repository's schedules are disabled after 60 days with no commits.' That workflow drives /api/cron/notify, /api/cron/lifecycle and /api/cron/warnings; .github/workflows/synthetic-check.yml:11-12 drives the synthetic check. vercel.json:9-18 carries only reconcile and usage, so 4 of the 6 jobs in lib/jobs/run.ts:49-55 live in GitHub Actions. lib/notify/alert.ts:58 shows alertOps enqueues rather than sends, so the alerts raised by app/api/cron/synthetic/route.ts:97-101 and app/api/cron/reconcile/route.ts:115-121 are delivered by the very drain that has stopped.
findings.why_it_matters: Sixty days of no commits is a normal gap for a one-author pre-revenue product. When the schedules switch off, delivery emails, expiry warnings, lapse transitions and the synthetic guest check all stop at once, and the alert that would tell you sits undrained in the notifications table. The customer-visible symptom is a couple who never receives the link to their wedding film, discovered by the studio rather than by you. The 401 detection at notify-drain.yml:106-111 only helps while the workflow still runs.
findings.fix: Move the schedule off GitHub Actions: either Vercel Pro's cron, or a free external pinger (Upstash QStash, cron-job.org) hitting the same routes with the same bearer. Until that is paid for, add a heartbeat in the opposite direction inside app/api/cron/reconcile/route.ts (a Vercel cron, which repo inactivity cannot disable): read getRepository().latestJobRuns(), and when the 'notify' run is more than two hours stale, send directly through the Resend driver rather than through enqueue().
findings.effort: 3 hours for the heartbeat; 1 hour to move the schedule once a scheduler is chosen

findings.title: No migration ledger and no CLI applier: schema changes go into production by pasting SQL into a web console
findings.evidence: scripts/migrate.ts:15-21 prints filenames and applies nothing; package.json:22 wires `db:migrate` to that printer. docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:114 concedes 'Which ones are already applied is a question the tables answer, since there is no ledger'. The two things that could answer it are both stale: lib/health/probes.ts:76-77 probes the credits table and calls it 'the newest migration's table (0021)' while supabase/migrations/0025_occasions.sql is the head, and scripts/preflight.ts:73 checks a hardcoded seven-table list that all comes from 0001. The sequence also skips 0003 with no record of why.
findings.why_it_matters: docs/NEXT.md:183-185 records that applying migrations on 12 September broke catalogue creation for the minutes before the deploy. There is no automated answer to 'is production on 0025?', no transaction boundary across a bundle unless a human remembers to wrap it (docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:112-113 asks them to), and no way for CI or the deploy script to refuse a build whose code needs a migration nobody has pasted. Every future schema change carries a self-inflicted outage window, and the risk grows with the number of live weddings.
findings.fix: Add supabase/migrations/0026_schema_migrations.sql creating schema_migrations(version text primary key, applied_at timestamptz, checksum text), and rewrite scripts/migrate.ts to connect over SUPABASE_DB_URL, read that table, and apply only unapplied files each inside its own transaction, recording the checksum. Then have app/api/health/route.ts report the max applied version, and make scripts/deploy-vercel.sh refuse to deploy when it is below the repo head.

findings.title: The usage rollup makes one sequential provider call per title in a single serverless invocation, with no maxDuration and no resume
findings.evidence: app/api/cron/usage/route.ts:47-68 walks every catalogue from listAllCatalogues(), then every title in each, awaiting provider.getUsage(title.providerId) one at a time. No route in app/ sets `export const maxDuration`, and vercel.json has no `functions` block. lib/jobs/run.ts:20-28 records a row only on normal return or a caught throw.
findings.why_it_matters: Today that is roughly 25 calls across 5 catalogues. At the documented target of ~10 weddings a month it becomes several hundred sequential HTTPS round trips to Bunny inside one function. When the platform kills the invocation on its duration limit, no job_runs row is written at all, so lib/health/probes.ts:180-186 reports 'Usage rollup: overdue' rather than 'failed' — and the delivered-gigabyte figures that quota enforcement and pricing depend on quietly stop being recorded, with the 300GB delivery alert (DELIVERY_ALERT_GB) never firing.
findings.fix: Add `export const maxDuration = 300` to app/api/cron/usage/route.ts, run the per-title getUsage calls in bounded parallel (a Promise.all over chunks of 8), and page listAllCatalogues() with a cursor carried in job_runs.detail so a killed invocation resumes rather than restarts. Do the same bounded-parallel treatment for the provider.getStatus loop in app/api/cron/reconcile/route.ts:50-99.

findings.title: No staging: a migration and the build that needs it meet for the first time in production
findings.evidence: docs/NEXT.md:181-194 describes N-87 and labels it 'debt that is costing us', noting that Vercel Preview has zero variables and lib/env.ts refuses a production build on an ephemeral driver, so no preview deployment can boot against anything real. scripts/deploy-vercel.sh:27 defaults TARGET to production. .github/workflows/ci.yml runs everything against memory and fake drivers (ci.yml:13-18) and never deploys anything.
findings.why_it_matters: Every deploy is the first time that build has run against the real Supabase schema, the real Bunny library and the real photo zone. The E2E suite — 212 tests, genuinely good — proves nothing about the combination that actually breaks, because it only ever runs against fakes. This does not cause a specific outage; it removes the only place any of the other findings here could have been caught cheaply.
findings.fix: Exactly as N-87 specifies: a second free-tier Supabase project seeded from the demo fixture, a second Bunny library and photo zone, a .env.staging.local pushed to Vercel's Preview environment by the same script with VERCEL_TARGET=preview, staging.mehfilbox.com on the preview branch, and `playwright test --base-url` so the suite can walk staging. Then make migrations-then-deploy run against staging first in the ship skill.

findings.title: The deploy script deletes each production variable before re-adding it, and does not strip quotes the way every other reader of that file does
findings.evidence: scripts/deploy-vercel.sh:79-80 runs `vercel env rm` then `vercel env add` for each variable. Line 74 takes the value as `value="${line#*=}"` with no quote handling, while scripts/preflight.ts:21 strips surrounding quotes with `.replace(/^["']|["']$/g, '')` — and Next.js strips them too when it loads .env.local. The script's own header (lines 6-8) claims the values pushed are 'the same ones the local verification scripts already proved work'.
findings.why_it_matters: A quoted value in .env.vercel.local is proved working locally and pushed to Vercel with the quotes attached, so the claim in the header is false for exactly that case. A quoted BUNNY_TOKEN_AUTH_KEY produces a green build and a 403 for every guest — the precise failure the script says it exists to prevent. Separately, a Ctrl-C or a network blip between the rm and the add leaves that variable absent, and because lib/env.ts fails closed the next build will not boot at all.
findings.fix: In scripts/deploy-vercel.sh, strip surrounding quotes from `value` with the same regex preflight uses, and replace the rm/add pair with `vercel env add "$name" "$TARGET" --force`, which upserts in one call and removes the window.

findings.title: Secret rotation has no path, and SESSION_SECRET is overloaded three ways
findings.evidence: SESSION_SECRET signs operator sessions (lib/auth.ts:26), signs fake-driver playback tokens (lib/video/fake.ts:61), and is the cron bearer fallback in all six cron routes (`env.CRON_SECRET ?? env.SESSION_SECRET`, e.g. app/api/cron/notify/route.ts:40). CRON_SECRET additionally lives in two unreconciled places: the Vercel project env and the GitHub Actions secret at notify-drain.yml:51. A grep for 'rotat' across docs/DEPLOYMENT.md and docs/GO-LIVE.md finds only an unrelated line about Bunny IP pinning (DEPLOYMENT.md:55). The only rotation tooling in the repo is scripts/rotate-operator-password.ts, which covers one operator's password.
findings.why_it_matters: If SESSION_SECRET leaks, recovery means signing out every operator and invalidating every passcode grant simultaneously, with no documented procedure and no dual-key support — and if CRON_SECRET happened to be unset, the rotation would silently change the cron bearer too. If BUNNY_TOKEN_AUTH_KEY leaks, every in-flight 4-hour playback token dies at once mid-reception. Neither has a runbook, so the response to a leak would be improvised under pressure.
findings.fix: Let SESSION_SECRET accept a comma-separated list in lib/env.ts (sign with the first, verify against all) so a rotation is a two-deploy operation rather than a mass sign-out; make CRON_SECRET required when DATA_DRIVER=supabase and delete the `?? env.SESSION_SECRET` fallback from the six cron routes; add a 'Rotating a credential' section to docs/DEPLOYMENT.md listing, per key, the blast radius and the order of operations.

findings.title: The cron authorization check is copy-pasted into six routes, compared non-constant-time, and is inert outside NODE_ENV=production
findings.evidence: The same four lines appear at app/api/cron/notify/route.ts:40-43, reconcile/route.ts:32-35, lifecycle/route.ts:22-25, usage/route.ts:34-37, synthetic/route.ts:37-40 and warnings/route.ts:23-26. Each is a plain `!==` string comparison guarded by `env.NODE_ENV === 'production'`. Nothing in tests/ asserts that a cron route performs the check.
findings.why_it_matters: The seventh cron route is one forgotten copy-paste away from being an unauthenticated endpoint that anyone can use to drain the notification queue or walk a catalogue. CLAUDE.md already identifies this exact shape as the risk for lib/admin/session.ts and lib/catalogue-access.ts — 'a route that does not call requireOperator is visibly unscoped' — and enforces the module registry with tests/unit/registry.test.ts. The cron surface got the pattern without the enforcement.
findings.fix: Add requireCron(request) to lib/http/ that reads env.CRON_SECRET and compares with crypto.timingSafeEqual, and have all six routes call it. Add a test in the style of tests/unit/registry.test.ts that globs app/api/cron/*/route.ts and fails if any file does not import and call it.

findings.title: /api/health cannot fail, and the Docker health check and the ship ritual both depend on it
findings.evidence: app/api/health/route.ts:12-21 returns `status: 'ok'` unconditionally and never touches the database; middleware.ts:12 excludes it from the matcher. Its `version` field comes from env.VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA (lib/env.ts:180), which is unset outside Vercel and falls back to the string 'dev'. Dockerfile:46-47 wires the container HEALTHCHECK to that endpoint, and .claude/skills/ship/SKILL.md:49 makes 'version matches the commit' the confirmation that a deploy is live.
findings.why_it_matters: A container whose Supabase project is unreachable reports itself healthy and keeps taking traffic, because the probe only proves the Node process answered. On the Docker path the ship ritual's version check degrades to comparing 'dev' against a commit hash, so the only automated proof that the right build is live is Vercel-only. The deep probes that would catch this already exist in lib/health/probes.ts but are reachable only from a logged-in platform admin page.
findings.fix: Add a `?deep=1` branch to app/api/health/route.ts that awaits probeDatabase(true) from lib/health/probes.ts and returns 503 when the state is 'down'; point the Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK at /api/health?deep=1; and add a BUILD_SHA env fallback in lib/env.ts set by the Dockerfile at build so `version` is meaningful off Vercel.

findings.title: The Docker path is the documented anti-lock-in story but is never built in CI and loses more than the doc admits
findings.evidence: A grep for 'docker' across .github/ returns nothing — no workflow builds the image, and Dockerfile's last change predates twelve migrations. docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:356-362 names three losses: wildcard TLS, the cron scheduler, and cross-instance ISR. Not named: lib/http/rate-limit.ts:16 holds rate-limit buckets in process memory (its own comment at lines 6-11 is honest that this is per-instance), lib/health/probes.ts:29 caches probe results in process memory, and .next/server/middleware-manifest.json shows NEXT_SERVER_ACTIONS_ENCRYPTION_KEY is generated per build, so two independently built images cannot serve each other's server actions.
findings.why_it_matters: The Dockerfile's own header (lines 4-7) frames it as insurance that 'our PaaS changed its pricing should never become their problem'. Untested insurance is not insurance: the first time it is needed will be under pressure, and it will fail on the crons (which must be recreated by hand) plus three per-instance assumptions the doc does not warn about. Meanwhile the passcode lockout that doc 05 §4 specifies becomes N times weaker behind N instances.
findings.fix: Add a job to .github/workflows/ci.yml that runs `docker build -t mehfilbox .`, `docker run -d -e SESSION_SECRET=... -p 3000:3000`, and curls /api/health, so the image cannot rot silently. Extend docs/DEPLOYMENT.md §10 with the three unlisted losses and a pinned NEXT_SERVER_ACTIONS_ENCRYPTION_KEY build arg.

findings.title: The one verification step in the ship ritual points at a hostname that is not production, and the deployment doc names three different production domains
findings.evidence: .claude/skills/ship/SKILL.md:46 curls https://marquee-film-pub.vercel.app/api/health. docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:273 says 'Production runs ROOT_DOMAIN=heirloomfilms.in', while .env.vercel.local sets ROOT_DOMAIN=mehfilbox.com and both workflows target https://mehfilbox.com (notify-drain.yml:52, synthetic-check.yml:30). docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:286-289 offers verification curls against admin.raammcorp.in and marquee.raammcorp.in. docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:251 claims .env.vercel.local 'holds all fifteen variables'; it holds 35.
findings.why_it_matters: scripts/deploy-vercel.sh:47-52 documents the exact incident this check exists to catch: a deploy that went to a second, empty project while production kept serving the old build, caught 'only by comparing /api/health to HEAD'. That check is now pointed at the old project's alias. A stale alias that still resolves returns a green, plausible health payload, so the ritual would report success for a deploy that went nowhere.
findings.fix: Delete the hardcoded host from .claude/skills/ship/SKILL.md and have scripts/deploy-vercel.sh curl the deployment URL that `vercel --prod` just printed, comparing `version` against `git rev-parse HEAD` itself. Fix docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:273, :251 and :286-289 to say mehfilbox.com and 35.

findings.title: .env.example is nineteen variables behind lib/env.ts, and the missing ones are the operationally load-bearing ones
findings.evidence: lib/env.ts declares 48 keys; .env.example lists 27. Absent from it: CRON_SECRET, NOTIFY_DRIVER, NOTIFY_FROM, RESEND_API_KEY, PHOTO_DRIVER, BUNNY_STORAGE_ZONE, BUNNY_STORAGE_PASSWORD, BUNNY_STORAGE_REGION, BUNNY_PHOTO_CDN_HOSTNAME, AUTH_DRIVER, DEMO_CATALOGUE_SLUG, ALLOW_EPHEMERAL_DATA, RECONCILE_STALL_MINUTES, PLAYBACK_TOKEN_TTL_S. docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:201-249 does cover most of them in prose, but PHOTO_DRIVER, RESEND_API_KEY and ALLOW_EPHEMERAL_DATA appear nowhere in that document at all.
findings.why_it_matters: The first artifact a cold-start engineer copies is wrong, and the failures are asymmetric. A missing CRON_SECRET means Vercel sends no Authorization header and every job 401s forever, which docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:243-247 correctly calls 'the one people forget'. A missing NOTIFY_DRIVER defaults to fake, which lib/env.ts:246-253 exists to prevent because it already shipped that way for a day and wrote rows marked sent that nobody received. envSchema is already exported at lib/env.ts:329 for exactly this kind of use.
findings.fix: Write a small script that walks envSchema's shape and regenerates .env.example with each key, its default and its description, and add a unit test alongside tests/unit/i18n.test.ts that fails when the file and the schema diverge — the same enforcement pattern CLAUDE.md already uses for i18n keys and module types.

findings.title: docs/GO-LIVE.md is a chronological log rather than a runbook, so the cold-start path is read-455-lines-and-infer
findings.evidence: docs/GO-LIVE.md:1 is titled 'Go live on heirloomfilms.in' — not the product's domain — and the file then appends two more go-lives at line 317 ('The Mehfilbox switch') and line 392 ('The second pass, deployed — 12 September 2026'), with steps marked '✅ done' in place (lines 49, 213, 359). Combined with docs/DEPLOYMENT.md's 456 lines and 24 SQL files that must be pasted by hand in order, the safe-deploy path for someone new is roughly 900 lines of prose plus manual DDL.
findings.why_it_matters: A cold-start engineer cannot tell which instructions are current, which are historical, and which were superseded — DEPLOYMENT.md:273 and GO-LIVE.md:1 disagree about the production domain, and both are written as fact. Realistically this is a full day to first safe deploy, most of it spent deciding which of two documents to believe, and the risk is that they follow a completed step and change something that is already right.
findings.fix: Split it: docs/RUNBOOK.md holding only the current procedure in present tense with no ✅ markers, and move the three dated narratives to docs/archive/go-lives.md, which CLAUDE.md's context-discipline rules already say is not read on the way in.
